items.title: Locally bounded distributional weak solutions of scalar laws
items.statement:
Let $T>0$, let $f\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be continuous, and let
$u_0\in L^\infty(\mathbb R)\cap L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R)$. A measurable
function $u\colon\mathbb R\times(0,T)\to\mathbb R$ is a **locally bounded
distributional weak solution** of $u_t+f(u)_x=0$ with initial datum $u_0$ if
for every bounded interval $I\subset\mathbb R$ and every $T'<T$ it is
essentially bounded on $I\times(0,T')$, and, for every
$\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R\times(-\infty,T))$,
$$ \int_0^T\int_{\mathbb R}\bigl(u\varphi_t+f(u)\varphi_x\bigr)\,dx\,dt +\int_{\mathbb R}u_0(x)\varphi(x,0)\,dx=0. $$
The integrals are local: if a test is supported in $I\times[-S,T']$ with $I$
bounded and $T'<T$, the local essential bound makes $u$ bounded on
$I\times(0,T']$, and continuity of $f$ makes $f(u)$ bounded on that bounded
range. The initial integral is finite because $u_0$ is locally integrable and
$\varphi(\cdot,0)$ is compactly supported. This is the local
integrability version of the weak identity in
[[def-distributional-weak-solution-of-a-scalar-conservation-law]], whose
published formulation assumes a global $L^\infty$ bound. This definition adds
no entropy inequality or strong local $L^1$ trace requirement.
items.strategy: Define the local essential-bound condition and weak identity for tests that may meet t=0.

items.title: Piecewise-constant finite-volume state and face-flux reconstructions
items.statement:
Use the cells, time levels, states and interface fluxes from
[[def-conservative-finite-volume-scheme]]. For $J_n^m=[t_n^m,t_{n+1}^m)$,
the **piecewise-constant state reconstruction** and **face-flux reconstruction**
are the measurable functions
$$ \mathcal U_m(x,t)=U_j^{m,n},\qquad \mathcal Q_m(x,t)=Q_{j+1/2}^{m,n} $$ whenever $(x,t)\in I_j^m\times J_n^m$. Values on cell or time-grid boundaries may be assigned arbitrarily, since those boundaries have two-dimensional Lebesgue measure zero. In particular, for almost every $(x,t)$, $$ \mathcal Q_m(x,t)=F\!\left(\mathcal U_m(x,t),\mathcal U_m(x+h_m,t)\right). $$
items.strategy: Define both reconstructions from the scheme and fix null-boundary conventions.

items.title: Godunov numerical flux for Burgers' equation
items.statement:
For Burgers' flux $f_B(s)=s^2/2$, define $G\colon\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R$ as follows. If $a\le b$, set
$$ G(a,b)=\begin{cases} a^2/2,&a\ge0,\\ b^2/2,&a<0\text{ and }b\le0,\\ 0,&a<0<b. \end{cases} $$ If $b<a$, set $$ G(a,b)=\frac12\max\{a^2,b^2\}. $$
This is the Godunov flux for the convex Burgers flux: for increasing states it
uses the minimum of $f_B$ on $[a,b]$, and for decreasing states it uses the
maximum of $f_B$ on $[b,a]$. It is proposed as a particular numerical flux in
the scheme of [[def-conservative-finite-volume-scheme]]. Its continuity and
consistency are verified in the pair.
items.strategy: Give deterministic case formulas for increasing and decreasing states.

items.title: The Burgers Godunov flux is continuous and consistent
items.statement:
The map $G$ defined in [[def-godunov-flux-for-burgers]] is continuous on
$\mathbb R^2$ and satisfies $G(a,a)=f_B(a)=a^2/2$ for every $a\in\mathbb R$.
items.strategy: Check continuity on open branches and switching boundaries, then verify the diagonal.

items.title: Discrete weak identity for a conservative finite-volume update
items.statement:
Let $(U_j^{m,n})$ be a scheme from
[[def-conservative-finite-volume-scheme]], with reconstruction
$(\mathcal U_m,\mathcal Q_m)$ as in
[[def-finite-volume-space-time-reconstruction]]. For a test function
$\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R\times(-\infty,T))$, define its space-time
cell average
$$ \Phi_j^{m,n}=\frac1{h_m\tau_m}\int_{t_n^m}^{t_{n+1}^m}\int_{I_j^m}\varphi(x,t)\,dx\,dt. $$ If $N\ge1$ is such that $\varphi$ vanishes for $t\ge t_{N-1}^m$, then $$ \sum_{j\in\mathbb Z}h_m U_j^{m,0}\Phi_j^{m,0} +\sum_{n=1}^{N-1}\sum_{j\in\mathbb Z}h_m U_j^{m,n} (\Phi_j^{m,n}-\Phi_j^{m,n-1}) +\sum_{n=0}^{N-1}\sum_{j\in\mathbb Z}\tau_m Q_{j+1/2}^{m,n} (\Phi_{j+1}^{m,n}-\Phi_j^{m,n})=0. $$
All sums are finite because $\varphi$ is compactly supported in space and time.
items.strategy: Multiply the update, telescope in time, reindex shared face fluxes in space, and retain the initial cell term.

items.title: Strong local convergence of consistent finite-volume face fluxes
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $(\mathcal U_m,
\mathcal Q_m)$ be reconstructions from
[[def-finite-volume-space-time-reconstruction]] for schemes using a continuous
consistent flux $F$ for a continuous physical flux $f$ as in
[[def-conservative-finite-volume-scheme]]. Suppose $h_m\to0$,
$\mathcal U_m\to u$ strongly in $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R\times(0,T))$, and
for every bounded interval $I\subset\mathbb R$ and $T'<T$ there is
$M_{I,T'}<\infty$ such that $|\mathcal U_m|\le M_{I,T'}$ almost everywhere on
$I\times[0,T']$ for every $m$. Then $u$ is locally essentially bounded up to
the initial face and, for every bounded interval $I$ and $T'<T$,
$$ \|\mathcal Q_m-f(u)\|_{L^1(I\times(0,T'))}\longrightarrow0. $$
items.strategy: Use spatial translation continuity, continuity on compact state ranges, and local control of the initial strip.
items.axiom_base: Assume only the Axiom of Countable Choice ACω, used in step 2.1 through the published L1 translation-continuity theorem for a compactly supported cutoff. No dependent or arbitrary-index choice is used.

items.title: Conservative finite-volume strong-limit theorem
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $T>0$, $f\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be continuous, $u_0\in L^\infty(\mathbb R)\cap L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R)$, and $F\colon\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R$ be continuous with $F(a,a)=f(a)$ for every $a\in\mathbb R$. For each $m$, form the conservative finite-volume scheme and space-time reconstruction of [[def-conservative-finite-volume-scheme]] and [[def-finite-volume-space-time-reconstruction]] using $h_m,\tau_m\to0$ and initial cell averages of $u_0$. Suppose reconstructions converge strongly in $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R\times(0,T))$ to $u$, and for every bounded interval $I\subset\mathbb R$ and $T'<T$ there is $M_{I,T'}<\infty$ such that $|\mathcal U_m|\le M_{I,T'}$ almost everywhere on $I\times[0,T']$ for every $m$. Then $u$ is a locally bounded distributional weak solution in the sense of [[def-locally-bounded-distributional-weak-solution]]; explicitly, for every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R\times(-\infty,T))$,
$$
\int_0^T\int_{\mathbb R}\bigl(u\varphi_t+f(u)\varphi_x\bigr)\,dx\,dt +\int_{\mathbb R}u_0(x)\varphi(x,0)\,dx=0.
$$
The strong convergence and local uniform bounds are hypotheses, not conclusions. No CFL condition or entropy inequality is assumed, so the theorem proves a weak limit only; it does not claim Kruzhkov entropy admissibility. If the limit is also globally essentially bounded, this identity is the published bounded weak formulation in [[def-distributional-weak-solution-of-a-scalar-conservation-law]].
items.strategy: Use discrete summation by parts, test-function quadrature estimates, strong state/face-flux convergence, and the initial boundary term; compactness and entropy are not conclusions.
items.axiom_base: Assume ACω, inherited only for the local spatial-translation step in the face-flux convergence lemma. The cellwise summation and passage to the weak identity use no further choice.

items.title: Godunov finite volumes preserve the Burgers shock speed
items.statement:
For $f_B(s)=s^2/2$, use the Godunov flux $G$ of
[[def-godunov-flux-for-burgers]] on cells of width $h_m\downarrow0$ with
$\tau_m=h_m/2$. Let $u_0(x)=1$ for $x<0$ and $u_0(x)=-1$ for $x\ge0$,
with cell-average initialization. The scheme preserves the stationary shock exactly:
$$ U_j^{m,n}=\begin{cases}1,&j<0,\\-1,&j\ge0.\end{cases} $$
Its reconstruction is the same stationary weak shock for every $m$. The
Rankine–Hugoniot speed is $0$, which is the speed of this limit.
items.strategy: Evaluate interface fluxes, show the update is stationary, verify the weak identity directly, and compute the jump speed.

items.title: Uniformly bounded cell reconstructions need not have a strong local limit
items.statement:
For $k\ge1$, let $h_k=2^{-k}$ and define the bounded cellwise functions
$$ V_k(x,t)=\begin{cases}(-1)^{\lfloor x/h_k\rfloor},&0\le x<1,\\0,&x\notin[0,1),\end{cases} \qquad 0<t<1. $$
Then $|V_k|\le1$, but $(V_k)$ has no strongly $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$-convergent
subsequence. These are a bounded sequence of cell reconstructions illustrating
why a compactness premise is explicit in the weak-limit theorem; they are not
asserted to arise from one fixed initial datum or from a stable update.
items.strategy: Show pairwise L1 separation on one compact space-time rectangle; no update trajectory is asserted.

items.title: A conservative consistent finite-volume weak limit need not be entropic
items.statement: Conservativity, diagonal flux consistency, local uniform boundedness and strong local $L^1$ convergence alone imply Kruzhkov entropy admissibility.
items.strategy: Prove the exact one-cell shift, local L1 convergence, weak limit, and direct entropy-inequality violation; the CFL condition fails.
items.axiom_base: Assume ACω, as required by the weak-limit and L1-translation suppliers; the entropy-defect calculation uses no further choice.
